It starts with a block, usually a rectangular prism, something so innocuous. But, with the block, there is potential. Potential to become the foundation of a great cityscape, beautiful wilderness, horrific battlefield, or simply a staircase to nowhere. Power is born from freedom, not complexity, and Blockland exemplifies this, all of the power lies within the players.
The potential of the block awakens this untapped beast in some, leading to beautiful constructions, ranging in styles and themes. Others tinker, looking to add to what's present, to add to the potential, changing how it works, from advanced RPG systems and finely tuned well-modeled guns to humble server tweaks and aesthetics, the community-made add-ons serve only to multiply what is possible in Blockland. In-game and out-of-game, Blockland has inspired true art and innovation, materialized into builds, and models, and scripts.
Above all in Blockland, the true strength lies within community. Not THE community, but of the concept of multiple people all in one place. I, for example, have made a number of friends from the game, though not every one has stuck around, we all shared something in common: Blockland. Unlike other games, the people of Blockland are generally more willing to form a bond with those they play with. But THE community, and by extension the concept of community in Blockland, are in a rut. Blockland needs our help.
Shame on other reviewers who say the game is good but lacks activity, shame on those who would abandon this game, even when they see the potential. Because this game will never become good unless multiple people come together to create, to inspire, and above all to have fun.
PROS:
-The power to create
-The ability to meet people
-Endless possiblities
-Devout players who still hold on
CONS:
-Low activity
-Negative Steam reviews turning people off from giving the game a FAIR CHANCE
-Transient players who try the game and drop it quickly due to low activity or bad reviews
-Negative feedback loop of player retention
In conclusion, in order to have fun in Blockland, the game needs people to ignore negative reviews, a community effort to return Blockland to its former glory. Current players should try to convince others to join or come back to the game, new players should pick the game up and really give it a go. Rather than tear down a game that's obviously bleeding, build it up, put in the effort until the bitter end.
People must look at Blockland, and see the potential that lies within, not superficial features. Because a simple block holds limitless potential, but if ignored it will remain just a block.

Disclaimer: I kickstarted this game, so I got to listen in on how the game was progressing in its final stages. This probably made me more inclined to like it from the get go.
That being said, it's a tough recommendation. There is a LOT in this game that is unpolished, and much of what makes the game interesting involves multiple playthroughs, or some save-slot shenaniganery to see how your choices actually change the story. Play through it only once, start to finish, and there will be a lot of questions left unanswered.
Particularly jarring are the transitions between game sections. When you finish a part, usually you'll get a text box to pop up that sums up what effects your actions have before moving on to the next scene, and often a new character, which is not unexpected. This is a text-based adventure game. But there's nothing else at the moment. At the very least I was expecting the background to fade to black, and the music to change to reflect the action that's now happening, even if we can't see it. But there's none of that, which felt extremely strange.
On a positive note, the setting is gorgeous for such a simple adventure game, the music (while a bit repetitive) is very atmospheric, and the characters are all well written and realized. If you can get into the game, it offers you some gut-wrenching choices to make.
Whether its worth $15 to you is completely subjective. But if it looks interesting to you, give it a look. Hopefully the folks at Pyrodactyl keep working and adding things to it, and I can give it a whole-hearted recommendation in the future.
Edit: I have run through the game again since they updated it, and the transitions are handled better. Consider that complaint solved.

It's a very good game. And it's FREE.
It's definitely not a Pay to Win.
It's definitely not a Pay to have access to game mechanics.
It's a Pay to have more Mechs.
I'll tell you my story. I still didn't spend a single EUR. Keep that in mind.
- Install the game
- Go on tutorial (I don't know why I did that, I played several Mechwarrior Games, but still)
- Make an extra tutorial mission.
- Abandon accademy
- Play about 10-15 games.
- check the Credits I accumulated
- Had about 18 millions.
So, what does this 18 millions means?
- Buy straight away a super strong Dire Wolf
- Buy a Timberwolf and have about 5m spare for the future or to buy loads of weapons to customize your deck
- Buy about 2 or 3 InnerSphere Assault or Heavy Mechs
So that's what you can get after 2 or 3 hours of gameplay.
After that point, starts the Grinding. But don't run away yet!
Recall that you have access 16 Trial mechs that are in real Mechs, it's just that you cannot customize them, but you can play with them.
At that point:
- make some Faction plays (where you deploy 4 Mechs and you have a specific mission to do)
- keep on doing Quick Plays with my Timberwolf
- earn money
- customize my mech further
- buy XP points to enhance my Mech
- make some Faction plays
- make some Quick Plays
Gather enough money to have a heavy customized Timberwolf and bought a Nova (Medium Mech)
At this point I'm earning about 800k credits during faction plays because I'm there with 2 Trial Mechs and 2 optimized mechs
An Atlas costs about 6 millions. So in less than 10 games I can buy a new Mech.
All this to say that yes there looks like being a grinding mechanic. But after a certain time, as you get better mechs, you earn more money, more quickly. And the Grinding stops.
The BS is gone, nothing but speed is left

This review will attempt to be biased towards gamers who are somewhere between competitive and casual.
MWO is a good team game.  You are in control of a mech for which you can customize the loadout, to fit your play style.  There are many chassis to choose from and many variants of each chassis with different hard points.
There are no bad mechs but there are also some mechs that are really good at one playstyle.  Mechs loadouts are secondary to player skill and team tactics.  Therefore a team of non meta builds can overpower a team of meta mechs at any point in time, if the players themselves are better.
Skill in this game is determined by positioning, aiming, and ability to maneuvre.  Each mech requires different positioning to be effective and the ability to aim while maneuvreing is an infinite learning curve.
With all that being said, this game offers a truly fun experience if you are willing to put in time to improve yourself.   You don't have to win to feel good about a match and if you can progress past the ideology that loadouts=win, then you will have a lot of fun.
The only downside to this game is the size of the community.  Because of the infinite learning curve, there would have to be 5x as many players in order for the match making tier system to truly work.  However, since players have been playing this game forever, day after day, new players are often discouraged from bothering to improve themselves, in the face of the elite players.  which means the community is not growing, despite a dedicated fanbase and active users.
If the community could grow, this game would take off.  Do not let this discourage you from trying the game.  You can still get into this game easily if you put in the time to learn.
Also, the p2w myth is a lie.  95% (guessing number up) of mech variants can be purchased for in game credits at a rate of about 1 mech per week of casual play.  The remaining pay wall mechs do not offer an advantage that another free mech could not also use.  They simply offer a way to save time in earning credits.

If you enjoyed Doom 1 and/or 2 then you're probably better off playing Doom 1 and/or 2.
Doom 2016 is kind of like an Adult Swim sketch, its' close enough to the source material to know what its' meant to be parodying but there's just enough distance from it that the writers have some creative freedom. If you're a fan of the older Doom games then you may not enjoy the new mechanics such as using "glory kills" to recover health rather than finding pickups, the kind-of-samey gore nest encounters and the fact that mobility and agility mean less when many enemies are accurate to the point of negating any benefit. The system of upgrading your character, his armour and his weapons, plus the platforming elements detract from the game's pacing. The respawn system can be difficult, as sometimes it will spawn you after a fight or in a new area if you die in the wrong place, and the feeling of power and strength that the original Doom games provided is never quite attained.
If I try to imagine it without the Doom title then I'd probably have enjoyed it more.

If you're new to Doom and you're looking for a challenging shooter then you'll probably like this game. If you liked Doom 3 then you'll probably like this game, but if you liked Doom 3 then you'll probably also enjoy drinking bleach.

Absolutely fantastic game. Glad all the years of them going through development for this paid off. I just wish I had the means to play it when it launched. Got it on the Autumn sale.
Pros:
-The gameplay is superb. It's super fast paced , high energy , quick shots , really tight mechanics. Just a lot of fun. Gives off an oldschool shooter vibe but made with modern FPS standards.
-Zones are usually really huge and you have plenty of space to work with. Some are small but it makes sense for the story.
-Lots of awesome guns. A staple of the series. Pistols, Shotguns, Lazers, Miniguns ,
, etc.
-AI is freakishly smart in certain situations and will try to group up around you in certain spots. Makes for a solid challenge and I promise you even on Normal , you'll die a lot till you get something right.
-Lots of checkpoints and save spots. Remember I said you'll die a lot? It's not too bad.
-Story line is a lot of fun , doesn't take itself too seriously yet is still very Interesting.
-The game has a ton of collectibles and secrets to discover. Powerups, Model viewers , Lore logs , etc. If you're into learning more about this universe/world the logs are great reads.
-Glory Kills are basically free kills when a demon glows. You can beat the living sh*it out of them in various ways. Even in the air. It's amazing and it rewards you with health and ammo. Feels great.
-Powerup system is nuts. If you're in a tricky situation and you grab one you become a god for like 10 seconds or more. Beserking is fuc*king awesome.
-Gun/Armor/Rune mods really shake this game up and let you play how you want. There's a challenge system in play as well allowing you to unlock points for these upgrades. I'll talk about that down this list.
-This art team is amazing. I was so impressed by how everything looked , the attention to detail was insane. So many little nooks and crannies to stop and look at it. Everything from high tech sci-fi to demonic shrines and blood pools with bodies hanging around everywhere. Crazy sh*it.
-Goes without saying but the enemies look and respond fantastically.
-The music is freaking bad a*ss. It's just faced paced metal and it's so sick to just run and gun while it's blasting. So good.
-
Cons:
*Some nitpicking*
-Challenges in this game range from fun to really annoying to pull off. Theres more annoying ones in this game. Like "glory kill this demon on this side , on this leg" or "kill three strong demons at the same time". It's easier said than done sometimes even with mods.
-Hell Knights. They're just so good compared to all the other demons. I'm not saying you can't kill them but sometimes they'll magically show up near you and backhand smack you. It's like a one or two shot kill on you. Other than that they're fine.
-Rune challenges are just "ok". Some of them are alright but the rest are not really fun. The runes themselves are great idea.
-I wish I could pick up and throw barrels. There I said it. Please add this if you ever make a sequel. Thanks.
Neutral:
-I haven't tried multiplayer yet as I type this. But I hear mixed things. Maybe I'll update this later if anybody reads this.
Anyways guys I highly recommend it. Solid game. Pick it up.

If you've played the other Sakura games, you've played this one. This VN is just one of many VNs that offer nothing beyond trying to entice the reader with ecchi. Every second this VN gets, they try to get the girls out of their clothes. Whether it be tentacle monster enemies (
burning their clothes (yes this happens) or the ill-fated beach trip, and even their outfits, this is a VN that focuses solely on ecchi.
The Sakura games forgo story and characters, so don't come into this game expecting anything gripping. You're given two girls in your choice of who to date, and both offer equally bland personalities, playing on the most one-dimensional versions of these anime tropes. I honestly forgot their names after a while, and just distinguished them with their character sprites. The good news is that the art is actually quite good, but that's about it. Both music and writing are horribly weak, and there are a lot of repeated scenes or just plain boring scenes that make going from one CG to the next real boring. If anything, this game was more of a chore to play through, ecchi or not.
The plot is you're...some agent in some city that fights...alien creatures with tentacles. And uh...your partners are both superpowered girls that either can make guns or clothes or have super strength. One is the collected type and the other a scatterbrain. The plot dragged along at a snails' pace and the girls offered nothing of interest so unfortunately, I don't remember remember much else.
Honestly, not worth the $10 this is currently going for. It's the same derivative things Winged Cloud has done for nearly ten games now, except even worse. This game is trying to pander hard without offering anything else, so unless you really want to see some 2D semi-nudity from these specific girls don't get this game. Just use Google if you need your 2D ecchi fix.

Okay, so, I am giving this a positive review because of the potential that lies for future iterations of this controller. For Valve's first attempt, I think this is a revolutionary controller, and it absolutely deserves to be refined further.
That being said, I use my Xbox One controller over this one all the time. But allow me to elaborate further.
This is a very different controller from conventional ones, in the best way possible. We've *needed* a controller like this forever, and we finally have one. Like I mentioned, this is a revolutionary controller, in the sense that it does a rather amazing job of combining the accuracy and precision of a mouse, with the ability to type on a very unique on screen keyboard, into a controller form factor. We've never had something like this, before. Valve's first crack at it is quite stellar. Valve, if y'all are reading this, as long as you keep refining and iterating on this controller, I will keep buying them, because the potential to become the ONLY controller you'll ever need is within reach.
However, in its current state, it's not an entirely practical controller. When I grab a controller, it's to simplify my gaming controls and to relax more. I don't want to have to think about configuration. Valve provides a mechanism to customize the living hell out of the controller, however, this requires time and effort. Now, you can grab community created profiles, and sometimes official profiles from game devs for the Steam controller, but I found that something would still feel off with those profiles and I would have to further tweak things to really feel comfortable. But again, that takes time and effort, and before I know it I found myself spending 15 mins just configuring the controller to play a game! The other issue is its plasticky feel. I know this is Valve's first piece of hardware, but the controller feels cheap in build. And this is a personal complaint, but if Valve scaled the controller down in size just a little bit more, it'd be perfect.
Even so, it's obvious that Valve's efforts to combat the problems I mentioned here can be refined further, and I think they're already partly tackling the problem with firmware updates to the controller and usability updates to Steam.
TL;DR: Buy this controller if you believe in the future of it and Valve, otherwise hold off for now.

Unrest is a text-based game set in a fantasy version of ancient India. You play vignettes in the lives of multiple characters, from a member of the royal family to a mercenary leader to a young peasant girl. Each story is short but interconnected with the others, and things that you've done as one character may come back to bite you while you're playing as another character. All of the characters feel like individuals, even the ones with only a few lines of dialogue, and the problems that these people are having don't have any easy solutions. Your characters gain "traits" based on how you play them. I don't think these traits actually do anything, but it was interesting to see them pop up because I felt like I was shaping who that this character was going to be from then on.
A full playthrough is relatively short (my first playthrough took two hours) though dependent on your reading speed, but there are so many choices to make that you'll want to replay it to see what you could have done differently.
The only complaints I have are small ones. I wish there was a tutorial or practice mode for the combat, I had a character die because I couldn't figure out how to turn him to face his assailant until it was too late. I also felt that the ending was a bit abrupt. It just cuts right from the final conversation to the credits and I was expecting a bit more. At the same time, I'm satisfied with how the playthrough turned out and I feel like the story had resolution, so it's not a huge complaint.

So I wasn't sure what to expect when playing through this game, I went in completely blind, but I was pleasantly surprised. The game is heavily text-based, so be wary of that before purchasing, it's not your typical modern RPG.
The closest thing I can compare it to is Heavy Rain. And that's a good thing. You have a lot of freedom within the choices you make and all of those choices can have heavy consequences. You play as multiple characters, and you can see the effects your choices from one character has on another, albeit never directly interacting.
The main game took a good 2 or so hours to complete, however with the amount of branching dialogue choices and I imagine endings too, that's pretty impressive. There's a lot of replayability here, especially with the mod support.
Closing words would just be to try the demo, it's there for a reason. If you like what you see, then the game will deliver!

Unrest is a story-driven, text-heavy adventure set in a fantasy version of India. You play as a group of different individuals, each with their own stories and problems in the world, and the choices you make greatly affect how each tale plays out. As you walk around and interact with the people around you, you'll learn information and make decision, which will ultimately lead each of your protagonists down good or bad paths.
If you're not the sort of person who likes text-heavy games, Unrest probably isn't going to win you over. If you do like your story games, though, this is well worth a punt. First of, the game has in My opinion a very shallow combat. You got 3 main weapon types: Kinetic(machine guns), Beams (obviously Lasers PewPew) and Missiles. Also, the ship building is very "uninterresting" for me. You got several hull types, obviously the bigger ones need research, and you just click how many Modules of what kind you want. This game is basicly just a machine that turns your Time into Frustration after you played it a while. Fun at first but becomes Boring, repetetive and uninterresting as you play it. I can only recommend it to Hardcore 4x Fans.

There was a small collection of die-hard fans playing almost daily and I kept seeing the same people in all of my matches.
Then the "Out of the Blue" update happened. It looked like they were coming back to try to balance out some things, but instead they watered everything down and removed the 9 classes from the game (3 light, 3 medium, 3 heavy) and instead made it some awkward mixture of customization where you selected your weight class and then equipped them with whatever weapons you chose, but some weapons weren't allowed to be used together (so basically they removed classes but tried to prevent players from combining the "best of" in a loadout).

I came into Tribes well after its glory days, but I was still there while people were playing the same game. That game is no longer around and instead there is just a shell of its former self that was watered-down in the name of "balance."

This game has a definite learning curve. It has a lot of hidden strategy and meta game that takes time to learn. You shouldn't expect to be very good when you start out and have just learned the basics. Aside from gameplay, it takes a decent chunk of time to earn credits, which you need to buy and outfit new mechs. This means that if you buy the wrong thing or make a bad decision, you will need to either get creative or start again from square one. If you arent self improvement oriented and dont see value in slow but steady progression, this game isnt for you. That being said, if you like the core gameplay (which is very intense and suspenseful, not to mention strategic), you will become addicted to this game. There is almost nothing else like it in the industry and boy is it ever a blast when you start really getting into it. That and the customization and how it effects combat is extremely gratifying. There are microtransactions and you are at a small disadvantage as a free to play user, but you are by no means handicapped to the point of not being able to be competitive. A good pilot in a terrible build will still do well. Skill is king.
I love this game. Its not for everyone and it may not be for you, but its definitly for me.

Mechwarrior Online - A Battletech game
Lies to you in its 4th and 5th words of its title.    It is a below average shooter loosely based on battletech ideas.
These ideas are poorly executed.
If you don't spend any money then this game is okay for what it is.
What it is, is a heartless product with no desire to increase core gameplay,  or  involve you (the player) with a story of what's going on, who's fighting,  and what are they fighting for.
If you spend no money playing this game, I would rate it a generous 4 out of 10.
If you are a founder, like myself, and paid waaaaaaaaaay too much then it is a 1/10.
Just beacause a niche monopoly exists on nostalgia doesn't mean you should abuse your fan base and the founders that dropped quite a bit of coin.
Pros
+ Good Mecha designs mostly
Negatives
- Poor server and hit registration.
- Cheaters went too long unchecked (eg Eglar, Faith)
- Current high tier players still "unchecked"
- Lost potential prizes for non-cheating players never compensated.
- Alt account abuse is rampant - eg Star Wolves
- No Bots
- No dedicated arena mode
- Faction warfare is drawn out and boring.
- Weapon variety is poor.
- Pinpoint focus allows spread weapons like missiles to behave like Autocannons
- New tech is patchy and rushed
- No support tanks, vehicles or infantry.
- Skirmish game mode is the same mode in other varities of modes
- Unbalanced map rotation
- Unbalanced maps
- Lack of maps
- maps are small
- NO PHYSICAL ATTACKS
- Clan mechs are more effective at brawling while Inner Sphere are better at range.  (It should be the other way around)
- No Oceanic servers for Faction Warfare, only North America

The is a fun, fast paced FPS. The grpahics are good. The response of the mechs vary with size and build adding a believability to it. The difference between a 100 ton mech and a 35 ton mech is glaringly obvious. The skill tree is fairly straight forward. If you have trouble with it there are plenty of user produced resouces to help. The intitial training is pretty informative for raw piloting. Developing the skill to be a good pilot does take a little time, but I enjoy a challenge. There is a grind, as well, to gain resources and experience. Many of the best mechs are reserved for pay to play. With that said, free to play players will find that over time they can build some pretty awesome mechs capable of handling those bought and paid for mechs. I have found that I am pretty proud of my mechs and want to spend money to make my mechs appearance unique on the battlefield... I suppose the developers need to eat too...
It should be noted that this is a team based game. Reguardless as to how good your mech is, if you do not work with the team your will be destroyed fairly quickly. Because of this, having a headset with a mike makes the game that much funner and your group more effective. Communication is essential. For the rambo types, light mechs are the way to go. Even then, it is still best to run in fast past groups and act like raptors.
The community is ok. There are cry babies who pout and whine when losing. Most are pretty cool people who are helpful. All my questions have been answered fairly quickly. Many are funny and witty. For the most part I enjoy interacting with other people who play this game.
There is no AI in this game. It is 12 v 12  players. Matching making varies. Sometimes mathes are started within a few seconds, at others it may take a minute. Very rarely have I seen 2 minute waits except in Fraction Play. It is always best to have a unit to play with in fraction play. All in all, I love this game.
I feel the f2p scheme this game has is fairer than most. The controls are relatively easy to get used to. The UI is pretty terribad, but the game itself is fun.

While I personally enjoy this game and have accumulated a large garage of mechs and equipment, I can't recommend it to new players. Once you get to where I am, the game becomes more enjoyable because you have plenty of c-bills to mess around with various builds, so if you have the patience to get to that point, have at it. Until then, the game is a slog.
Aside from the grind, the game itself is horrendously slow and unoptimized. Load times are long. After each patch it just gets more and more slow. I think the problem is the devs don't have the original documentation on the source code, and their original engine programmers have long since left, and no one currently on the dev team can do anything to optimize the engine. So all they can do is make bandaid patch after bandaid patch, piling on a bunch of new mechs and "features" until eventually the game itself will crumble under its own Jenga-like pile of code. Maybe someday they'll rebuild the game on a new engine and keep proper documentation this time, but that's just wishful thinking. PGI is not known to be the most competent developer.
Also, the community is absolutely cancerous. Most of the dying community is made up of autistic old men who think they know what they're doing and get offended when you point out that maybe their mech builds and strategies aren't the best, and this incompetence often leads to one-sided matches. To make matters worse, the moderation is like a totalitarian police state and will ban you from the game entirely for the most inoffensive things, or they pass judgement without checking the content at all and just go by the mass reports sent by the butthurt manchildren you called out for dragging your team down with their ineffective builds or strategy. Deus is to me one more time!  OK, so, it was obvious that this game set out with a single goal:  to take Deus Ex, a game that some people claim is the greatest game ever made, and bring it up to date with modern graphics and better game-play.  Well, did they succeed?  Sort of.  First off, the game does, indeed, look great.  Some of the visuals are a little less than inspired, and there is a little repetition, but that's only slightly annoying.  Overall, they keep the graphics fresh and interesting while making the game -feel- a lot like the vaunted Deus Ex progenitor.  And, it does feel a lot like Deus Ex 1.  I would say, almost that it's hard to make sense of the design choices without playing Deus Ex 1 and experiencing the quirkiness thereof.  But, there are two things that make the first Deus Ex so great...interesting gameplay and an even more interesting plot.  Now, this game has an ok, plot...above average certainly, but it's hard not to invite comparison.  Wheras the first Deus Ex dove head first into the interesting territory of X-files meets internet conspiracies about world government and the illuminati, this game barely touches the issue, as though it's just a little afraid.  And, this just does irreparable damage to the plot (By the way, this game's theme is basically the same, worn out theme from the X-men and similar...we're powerful so people fear us, blah, blah, blah).  The first Deus Ex had no such fear...you start out as the Black Helicopter riding secret agent of the UN killing separatists.  So, why the fear now?  Is this watered down for the international market?  Is there a conspiracy?  OK, I'll stop now, but you get my point:)  The plot was semi-interesting at points (and the character development was well conceived) but could have been so much better.  Human Revolution was a bit short, even with the ex-pac jammed in there.  Oh, and jammed in there it is!  When you play through this level, you'll be annoyed (at least) the entire time.  I've never seen so poorly integrated an expansion in my life.  The expansion is good (enough), especially in terms of game play (cause the plot in kind of so-so as well), but wow was this a square peg pounded mercilessly into a round hole.  Oh, and the choices you make in this game are great:)  Your character is customizable, the choices have real consequences.  This part of the game was really well done.  Overall, this is definitely worth playing.  It's not quite the spiritual journey of Deus Ex 1, but it's definitely a little redemption for Deus Ex 2.

This has to be one of the most infuriating games I've ever played. If it was less sadistic it'd just be a mediocre shooter. As it stands it's entertaining to play if you're a glutton for punishment and want the challenge of seeing the game to completion. I cannot say I recommend it, but it can be enjoyed in a weird way. There are certainly a lot worse games you can get on Steam for 74 cents (what this was on sale for).
The main difficulty in this game comes from its damage model. On Normal difficulty, a headshot is an instant kill, a body shot takes about 2-5 hits depending on the weapon, then limbs and finally hands/feet do less. This also applies to you, so you will be killed within seconds or instantly if some of the enemies firing machine guns at you from far away get a lucky headshot. Something that's really neat is that there are ricochets, but in practice this just means the enemies mindlessly emptying their 72-round machine guns can kill you when you're behind cover near ricochet-able walls.
Another challenge in the game is aiming. The enemies reflexes are amazing and they will start firing before you can get out of cover enough to aim. Occasionally you can angle yourself in such a way that you can fire at their limbs without being seen, and you need to take these opportunities when you can. You cannot use the iron sights on your weapons so long-range combat is difficult even with a rifle. You just have to aim your crosshair for center mass and hope for the best.
The enemy AI is, well... non-existent. They run from their spawn positions, if scripted to do so, and then stand in place immediately firing at you when you come into sight, emptying their magazine. There is rarely the opportunity to sneak up on an enemy from the side or behind, so you will have to quickly duck out from cover as they reload and get a few shots off hoping you don't get hit. Defeated enemies will randomly drop first aid kits which restore 10 of your 100HP. Getting shot once can take anywhere from 5-25 so it's very difficult, but necessary to take down most enemies without taking damage. Quick save/load abuse is mandatory.
Depending on how lucky you are with combat, the game is about 4-6 hours long. The levels mostly involve close-quarters combat with a bit of obstacles like rooftop ledges or vents (aka ricochet 'heaven'). The game is cruel, so it will sometimes spawn enemies behind you after passing certain points in the levels. There is one vehicle segment and the last two levels in the game are escort missions. These are by far the least enjoyable in the game.
The vehicle level is buggy beyond belief
It starts off by you being driven in front of a vehicle with four machine-gun toting enemies. Half of the time they will kill you before you can even get your crosshair over them. The car then stops in a position where two of the enemies are outside of you aiming range, so you have to blow up their vehicle by emptying two AK clips into it. It is a matter of luck if you can do this before the two enemies kill you. Then comes the bugginess... all of the other vehicles in the level seem to have about a 25% chance of spawning correctly. You will then be chased by a rolling tire, which is invulnerable and will crash into your vehicle causing it to explode. If you quick-save and then quick-load multiple times, your game will either crash or sometimes a black car will spawn instead (albeit missing a tire) and you can kill the vehicle before it crashes into you. Thankfully the other invulnerable tires in the level will not cause your vehicle to explode and the level will end. If you should be unlucky enough for a further two vehicles to spawn correctly, there will be eight enemies which you cannot aim at firing at you and killing you. This time you will want to quick-save and quick-load to prevent those from spawning.
Apart from the vehicle mission, the game is playable. The escort mission is like a normal level except you have a slow, wounded guy following you. The enemies ignore him and he stays out of the way of their fire, which is nice, BUT every few minutes the game spawns an enemy soldier close to him that runs up to him and empties his machine gun into him. So while you're worried about saving your own skin, cowardly ducking behind cover with an onslaught of four machine guns firing at you, you also have to babysit.
On a lighter note, the voice acting is hilariously bad and you occasionally catch soldiers having conversations about you before you engage them. It's a bad game no doubt, but I came in with low expectations and got some enjoyment from it.

The Stalin Subway 2: Red Veil replaces not only protagonist, but also the fun with frustration. Previously in my adventures in the black hole of Orion Games, I enjoyed The Stalin Subway for its schlocky yet, classic approach to FPS games. While the Red Veil shares much in common, the sense of effort is clearly missing in this sequel.
Exactly the same as its predecessor. Nearly everything here is reused from the original game apart from the HUD. That's not entirely a bad thing, The Stalin Subway/Red Veil isn't a bad looking game, but some new things to look at would have been nice.
While the controls and overall gameplay stay the same, Red Veil removes some features from its former glory for... what purpose I don't know. The armor meter is gone, though you think that wouldn't be a problem because SS1 almost never gave you any armor anyway. However, it is sorely missed here. Enemies seem to have extremely inconsistent damage output ranging from 2% of your health, to nearly 100% of your health at any given moment.  This makes each gun fight a roll of the dice, and can possibly leave you with a nearly impossible chance of surviving your next encounter.
The enemy AI itself is heavily scripted. Upon spotting you or reaching it's scripted position, the enemies will stand still and unload entire magazines in your direction until they are forced to reload. This is both highly predictable and abusable. It also breaks the entire pace of the game as you spend 5-10 full seconds waiting around a corner listening to 2 men empty their 72 round drum mags at a wall.
All reused asset here again for gameplay sounds. Guns still sound weak, unfitting to their rugged and powerful real-life counter parts. The soundtrack in Red Veil is actually its brightest spot. There's several tunes in the game that I will put in my playlist shortly. The voice acting is.. Amazing. Really, this is undoubtly worse and just as legendary as the original Resident Evil. Do yourself a favor and find these cutscenes, they'll make your day!
You play as the wife of the original protagonist of The Stalin Subway; Lana Survorova. As an ex-high ranking officer in the KGB, you and your husband are being hunted down by your former employers. Gleb, her husband, is captured and Lana must rescue him before they make their escape from Moscow... That is the entire story.
The amount of levels in Red Veil pales in comparison to it's predecessor which had 32 levels. There are just eight, EIGHT missions in the game and it will take you barely over an hour to complete the entire adventure.
The Stalin Subway 2: Red Veil isn't a sequel, its a single player expansion. Had I paid more than the $0.82 I did, I probably feel ripped off. Even For fans of the original; it's a short, frustrating, and disappointing experience.

This game is fine-- it's objectively fast-paced and intense in a specific way that's an antidote to most other shooters going right now, and that alone is probably enough to recommend it to anyone looking for a different flavor of FPS, or anyone who already loves that style of shooter and wants More. There's a lot of extra content too in terms of challenges and secrets that are actually hard to find and making your own maps and the arcade mode and all the rest of it, so if you like the game you'll find a lot to keep your occupied. But writing from the perspective of someone with limited time to play games who thus values more than just gameplay, i would say give this game a pass if you're in the same boat - it's fun, but it's JUST fun. And it's not even all that fun, to be honest.
Numerous fundamental issues start to build early in the game: a game engine known specifically for texture pop-in is blatantly the wrong choice for a game so fast-paced, and you'll be reminded over and over; enemy design that doesn't take into account the environments the enemies will appear in, so the enemies don't stand out from the backgrounds, and moreover the game is too fast to ever really take in their detailed designs; the weapon balance is completely off, in the way that it wasn't in 1994 Doom, and so you'll just end up using one or two weapons instead of picking different guns for different scenarios; similarly, the enemy balance is off too, too many things are Fast And Nimble, hit points seem to have been allocated randomly so some enemies are way too tough and some too easy; some of the weapons take up way too much room on the screen so it looks like you're piloting a spaceship when you pull out your chaingun; the ammo and other pickups look boring and too similar; unforgivably, the game has LESS atmosphere than Doom 3, largely due to a tongue-in-cheek presentation (the UAC hologram guys) that saps it of all seriousness and leaves everything as just set dressing; and most unforgivably of all the game knows that nobody cares about the story in a Doom game and then includes one anyway - a severely half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥one filled with boring, motiveless villains and bush-league writing - thus pleasing neither the people who care about stories nor the ones who don't. Fundamental issues, one after the other, leading to a game that you WILL find annoying if you care about attention to detail or thoughtfulness or story or anything beyond sheer gameplay. Issues that make this game not worth your time if you need art to be thoughtful and inspiring and well-crafted. It's maybe the last time i try a AAA game, to be honest, because it's always the same story of acing the easy stuff and then doing such a thoughtless job of more nuanced things because even the designers have accepted that "it's just a game."
Again, in terms of sheer gameplay Doom is a winner -- every game does one thing better than any other game, and Doom has fast and intense gameplay that you will NOT find in any comparable modern FPS. But that's all it has, and moreover it has fast and intense gameplay that you can easily find in many OLDER games - games like the Serious Sam series that do not have a huge list of fundamental design problems - and even if you specifically like the sci-fi concepts of futuristic Mars bases and demon portals and all that creepy stuff then you are, improbably, much better off playing Doom 3, which has its own issues but at least brought those concepts to life with a very convincing atmosphere (including a much Hell-ier Hell). Play this game if you want more of this kind of gameplay, but not for any other reason - it won't inspire you with its attention to detail, it won't convince you that games are an art form, it won't impress you with knowing when to shut up and when to tell a story, and it won't change your life by showing you a perfectly balanced game experience that could be built upon in the future. It'll just show you why the original Doom is still good today: because it got the fundamentals right in a way that way too few people have chosen to learn from. Just because it arrived later doesn't make it evolution.

This is the most versatile and customizable controller ever made. It works for practically every game, with fps games you can use the gyro and touchpad together to get quick aiming and accuracy. The touchpad is also nice for strategy games and a nice alternative to using a mouse. Typing on it can be tedious but that's not really what it was meant for. You can customize every single aspect of the controls, map any key or touchpad click to a keyboard button, and that's just basically scratching the surface.
Switching back over to the mouse after a month or so of mostly using it, I seemed to gain around a 15 to 20% accuracy boost while playing Warframe. So you know, the mouse is always going to be faster and more accurate, but keep in mind that I've been using a mouse and keyboard for years, so maybe after a year or so that could change, I was surprised at how accurate it can be. The controller feels so nice and is so entertaining to play games with overall, it was definitely worth the price in my opinion.
Oh yeah the battery life is ridiculous, I've been using this thing for just over a month now and I've still not changed the batteries once, granted I haven't been purely using the controller during that time, but it's impressive nonetheless.
Big picture mode can be a bit annoying at times though, and you pretty much have to use it with the controller, so keep that in mind as well. And if you don't have internet, you basically can't use the controller, also it works exclusively with Steam. Those negative aspects are microscopic to me in the grand scheme of the controller though, since I've never really had any issues with them, I'm always with internet and steam.
Nice controller, but could definitely be better.

Xbox did things right when they released their controller for the 360 and again for the Xbox 1. These controllers aren't perfect but they're cheaper than the Steam Controller and arguably offer easier control and more precision.
Keyboard and Mouse are still the best. Now some games aren't designed to be used with a keyboard and mouse, and those games are almost always better played with a controller. However, the vast majority of games on steam are best played with a keyboard and mouse. Most modern games allow you to easily re-bind any keys you like, and a keyboard/mouse will always allow for the best customization.
The Steam Controller does hit a niche that the xbox and keyboard/mouse combos don't, but this niche is very small. Having the latter two controllers will be more than sufficient for most gamers, so save your money instead.
The Steam Controller has very well supported software to go along with it. It functions very smoothly with steam and especially big picture mode, and I suppose that would make it a good couch controller.
Unless the Steam Controller becomes cheaper than the 360 or Xbox1 controllers, I don't see much of an application for any serious gamer.

This has to be an experiment to see if a game can be as just as annoying or more annoying than it is fun. Everything it has going for it is matched by some downside. Here we go:
It looks pretty good - even by today's standards for a little top-down game the environments and explosions are lush. If they had dynamic lighting it would look amazing. But it introduces these good looking environments with unskippable cutscenes (I mean the in-engine ones, thankfully you can skip the comic ones). In an arcade game. What?
You have several characters to pick from with different abilities and upgrade paths, nice. But they have zero personality and you have to deal with a hyper annoying gung-ho order-barking boss that I really wish could be silenced.
The core game mechanics are pretty tight - drive your little vehicle, shoot things, get better guns, shoot things some more, sometimes change to some other vehicle, shoot even more things. That's good in small doses... but this game basically keeps on stacking more and more and more on top of a level. It all takes forever to finish (seriously, it feels like a level goes on for an hour or so, even if it doesn't really) and if you don't succeed you'll start all over again.
Well, that was the good stuff... what else is annoying - random falling damage - who knows if you'll survive this jump? Your vehicle clips on things or flips over quite easily. Once again - your idiot boss has just one answer to all of life's problems - blow it up - and he'll use every single chance to yell it out to you. Achievements are once again more annoying than interesting, forcing you to juggle tasks within the timed missions. There's more, but this is already long.
So why recommend it? Well, if you like this sort of game there aren't many options on PC. It does look good, things do blow up quite nicely and you do power things up so the missions start to flow a little faster. If you are ready to grit your teeth a good deal give it a try.

Please ignore the limited time spent in game, as I discovered the reason for my review in the extra research I did after purchasing the game on sale.
In short, in a game that is very like SotS, Civilizations, and SoaSE (which have teams,) there are no teams (only temporary alliances) and only one player can win. You cannot win with a friend, and will eventually have to either crush them or just quit the game. In all fairness to the developer and players who think this is a piddly reason for a negative review, consider this. Many players purchase games like this specifically to play with their friends, and it should be a relatively easy thing to add, so how could both they and we benefit from such a move???
Quite simply this is because the game has been out for 5 years and Disharmony out for 3, so this change is most likely never going to happen, nor will it happen 1 year after its launch like it should've.
To those who say this would've broken the game:
1. It would also be easy to lock this feature to Singleplayer and Private Multiplayer to keep it out of public servers.
2. It will not break YOUR game, it will only break the games of those who CHOOSE to use team systems.
To those who say  it wasn't worth it, there were two bonuses there:
1. Adding Co-op to the tags opens up the game to a wider market, not only to players with co-op friends but also to less strategic minded players who wouldn't be able to win singleplayer without a bot on their team.
2. The change would detract froms reviews like this.
To those that think co-op is dumb for this game:
1. Sins of a Solar Empire
2. Civ 5
3. Sword of the Stars
4. Galactic Civilizations II
5. Supreme Commander (V and FA)
Name one, RTS or 4X, that doesn't benefit experience-wise from playing with your friends.

Tribes: Ascend is a multiplayer-only online arena high-speed first person shooter. It’s an everlasting factional warfare between the Blood Eagles and Diamond Swords set in the distant future. These tribes are battling it out for ultimate supremacy in a futuristic Sci-Fi universe where the fighting seems unlikely to stop anytime soon. In-game, this simply affects the color of your armor, the announcer’s voice and where you spawn. Three different armor bases form the basis of what a player can and can’t do at any one time. There are a wide variety of different weapons ranging from explosive projectile weapons, hitscan assault weapons to sniper rifles and more. There are five distinct game modes and more than 40 maps combined spanning these modes. These maps are huge, allowing for high speed build up and action on a giant battleground. Each map is designed with its mode in mind and only share the general aesthetics. There is an official rule set for each mode but you can also set up your own server with custom rules. T:A sets itself apart from other first person shooters with high speed skiing, jet pack action and projectile preference over hitscan weapons. It’s free-to-play which means that T:A has a decent variety of skins and voice packs to customize your look as well. Is it worth checking out? Well, let’s talk about the shooting elements next.
With the Out of The Blue Patch, Hi-Rez has clearly shown that it has learned from the mistakes of the past. The huge amount of grinding is gone, the weapon play feels more balanced than it ever has in the past and Tribes is fun to play again. Despite its quirks and imperfections, Tribes still has something to offer after three years. It’s hard to deny the rush you get when you’re skiing at 300 km/h across the map while dodging all sorts of projectiles thrown your way. The increased flexibility with loadouts makes for a much more interesting play/counterplay setup if the rest of your team is on the ball. I’m not 100% sold on the current weapon or armor balance right now. It’s definitely better than it used to be but some of them, like the bolt launchers, feel superfluous or heavies are a little too good. However, it’s no longer a hitscan nightmare fest that it used to be. Where paid players had a clear advantage over free players. I’ll be curious to see how patches over the months and possibly years go. So far, they seem to be keeping the game going at a regular, if slow, pace.

Hi-Rez returned in December to give T:A a much needed overhaul in balance and several new maps for players. But that will probably be the exception to the norm. Since then, there’s been smaller bug fix patches, a new map here and there and minor balance changes to address community complaints. Tribes: Ascend seems to be a passion project for Hi-Rez and as such I would temper one’s expectation of regular content. Unfortunately, the Out of the Blue update did not create a substantially larger player base. There was a big jump in players when they announced the patch, but it has since returned to the normal small levels it had before the patch. Even so, the game is playable now without the major issues that used to plague it. I’d say you’ll get about 5-8 public servers going on any particular day. So, there’s always something to do. For now, it seems like Hi-Rez plans on supporting the game for the foreseeable future with small updates to keep the game going.
Out of the Blue shows how much Hi-Rez studios has grown since its screwup with Tribes: Ascend. Many of the balance problems are fixed, the large amount of grinding is gone, the business model feels a lot more fair and there’s more content to enjoy. Capture the Flag is clearly the focal point of T:A and its still really fun to play. This is the best state the game has ever been in despite its flaws. The community is still pretty decent too. However, said community is small and may not grow anytime soon unfortunately. There are some aspects of balance that may need to be adjusted as time goes on and I would like to see more content released. Deus Ex: Human Revolution is easily one of my favorite modern video games. It is one of the few games that I feel offers a good balance of compelling storytelling and deep gameplay. Like with most video games, the story isn't amazing, but it was interesting enough to keep me invested in the outcome. The gameplay, of course, is the main draw and it is some of the best I have experienced in a modern game (within the last 10 years). It offers freedom in a way few games do. Your actions really matter - even the smallest, seemingly inconsequential decisions you may make can have major effects. Unlike other games with a lot of freedom in choice, the decisions you make impact the gameplay significantly. These choices may not be the morally wrenching ones you see in other games, but be sure (whether you make an ethical, morally gray or unethical choice) it will affect the gameplay going forward. The Director's Cut is the most complete version of the game and it addresses many of issues found in the original release. There is no reason to not buy the Director's Cut.
Overall, Deus Ex: Human Revolution is a great game that has a lot to offer both those looking for deep/open-ended gameplay and a cinematic story experience. The only avenue I could see myself not recommending it is to people who don't enjoy science fiction stories and settings. Otherwise, enjoy!

Deus Ex: Human Revolution was my first game in this title and I absolutely loved it. It made me want to play other Deus Ex games and actually had me strapped to a chair and watching youtube videos about the past games to better understand the lore.
The game's visuals are stunning. The setting the atmosphere, everything is very well designed.
The story is breathaking. You are flung into a corporate espionage, conspiracies, illuminati and personal vendetta. Your loyalties and moral compass will be constantly under check.
The gameplay itself is solid, especially for it's time. It needs some getting used to, however. You can stealth your way through the area, or go full RAMBO. Either way, it is up to you.
Sneaking about and finding different places, secret locations grant you good rewards. Hacking is important as it grants access to  good stuff.
The progression system is great and it actually matters. It changes the gameplay for you. At first you will be finding ladders to get down from heights, but if you invest in the Ikarus landing system, you can jump off from anywhere. Invest heavily in hacking, and you'll have an easier time.
Overall, it's a great game. Very intense. The dialogues are spot on, you can persuade people to do what you want and so on. Your actions, have consequences.
One problem, I found was that the stunningly beautiful backgrounds... are just backgrounds. You look at the upper city and want to go there, but you can't.
Bullets, are also very hard to come by. You'll have to manage your inventory well. That adds a little realism.
Boss battles are very underwhelming though. Stay moving, and shoot with the biggest gun you have. That's how you kill every single boss, except the last one.
8/10

It was actually pretty good at first, but you need to collect experience points to unlock new guns to disassemble. Or you could pay to unlock every gun instead. So, your patience or your wallet, you decide. In short, ♥♥♥♥ YOU Noble Empire Corp. This didn't have to be a free-to-play game, you just couldn't help yourselves.

If you find guns interesting,  or some vehicles maybe, or want to play a puzzle game where you don't only have a few levels with time challenge and leaderboards, this game is for you. Successful disassembly requires removing parts in correct order, of course. Point & click. Assembly: reversed order. Simple. Doing it fast, however is extremely hard.
Easy daily challenges will help you slowly gain more xp if you are stuck.
It's F2P with microtransactions, so:
Unless you spend your whole life completing challenges  and are very freaking good at it (Some guns require credits, which are earned by achieving a daily high score), you will have to buy credits, which are fairly cheap. Unlocking is also cheap if you have sufficient xp. Vehicles are unreasonably expensive.
If  you want to suggest a model it will cost you way too much and will only be accepted if it receives a thousand votes. Xbox did things right when they released their controller for the 360 and again for the Xbox 1. These controllers aren't perfect but they're cheaper than the Steam Controller and arguably offer easier control and more precision.
Keyboard and Mouse are still the best. Now some games aren't designed to be used with a keyboard and mouse, and those games are almost always better played with a controller. However, the vast majority of games on steam are best played with a keyboard and mouse. Most modern games allow you to easily re-bind any keys you like, and a keyboard/mouse will always allow for the best customization.
The Steam Controller does hit a niche that the xbox and keyboard/mouse combos don't, but this niche is very small. Having the latter two controllers will be more than sufficient for most gamers, so save your money instead.
The Steam Controller has very well supported software to go along with it. It functions very smoothly with steam and especially big picture mode, and I suppose that would make it a good couch controller.
Unless the Steam Controller becomes cheaper than the 360 or Xbox1 controllers, I don't see much of an application for any serious gamer.

Quick overview of fixes for common starting bugs, basically so people don't downvote the game because of these -
- Audio Crackling, if this happens go to your audio playback settings and set it to 24 bits 48000HZ.
- Slow Motion, this was caused by setting the game to 60fps for me and the sure fix was setting it to 30 again. Not a problem everyone has with 60fps but try 30 if you have it just incase.
- Achievements and other info locking into black bars, this is simply cause by Steam Overlay. Just go to Library -> Right click game -> Properties -> Disable Steam Overlay.
- Game not loading in Fullscreen after setting it to On previously, just turn it off and back on again. Also if this does not work go to your config.ini file in Naruto file and change windowed to 0, even if it already says 0 delete and retype it.
Enjoy :)

Cities in Motion 2 is a great instalment in transportation simulators. The game is very simple and is, though sometimes tedious, very fun. Once you set your transportation empire going the sky is the limit. You can make routes for several public transport vehicles. You can make a bus line (good for short distances). You can make a trolley (looks cool). You can also, my favourite, make a tram line (very simple and fun). There are also metro and waterbus lines, these are very complicated and take a lot of logistics to maintain and plot. Great game and I highly recommend it!

The original Cities in Motion was already a great cousin to business sims like the legendary Transport Tycoon, but the sequel really kicks it up a notch. Since you can build roads SimCity style, it now feels more like a city simulator restricted to running the department of transportation than a straight-up business simulation. It has a lot more depth (like the timetables and depots), but it doesn't take long to get the hang of what's new. If you enjoy business simulations, this is a must-have for your collection.

It is one of those games that specialises for a niche market instead of trying to be some generic AAA title. Does the idea of building tram/metro lines, placing stops, setting up lines and fine tuning timetables sound fun to you? No? Then you will not enjoy cities in motion. That is fine. However if you love that kind of micro management, monitoring how well your transport network is doing with charts and looking forward to your next optimised transport route then this game will keep you up all night!

Cities in Motion 2 is the sequel to the popular mass transit simulation game Cities in Motion. Build, manage and lead your transportation network to provide cities with their ever changing needs. CIM2 introduces new features including multiplayer game modes, day and night cycles, timetables and dynamic cities.
Building the transportation network will directly affect how the city grows. Affordable transportation brings middle class housing and work places, while more expensive and exotic choices bring high end businesses. Take advantage of many different types of vehicles including buses, trams, ferries and more.
Build alone or play cooperatively with a friend. Use the newly implemented bus lanes to build efficient traffic free roadways. Tackle rush hour by managing transportation timetables and meeting the needs of the citizens.

CONS

5. Flashbacks
It's basically cheap voice acting. The images are re-used over and over again.

This game is kind of a guilty pleasure for me. I just completed it on normal difficulty and I honestly can't believe that it got released with all the problems the game mechanics have. Everything you can possibly imagine that could be wrong with a first person shooter is done in this game. There is a rail section where you are in the back seat of a vehicle being shot at with no way to dodge or duck. If you start the mission with anything below 100% health, (meaning you have to complete the previous mission with 100% health) than you might as well reload an older save file and start from a previous mission. There is a sewer level where the water rises, but if you stay underwater too long, you lose health. The problem is that the damage taken for lack of oxygen while being under water is accumulative, meaning that if you begin losing health after being underwater for 10 seconds, and you emerge for air after 9 seconds, going back under the water (which is required) will start to hurt you after being submerged for only 1 second. The game finally concludes with what I can only describe as one of the worst escort missions in FPS history. The only good thing I can think to say is that there were no timed missions.
Well, the game's not all bad. Let's talk about what they did right. First, the game is short, (a good thing in this case). Second, there is a very convenient quick save and quick load feature, so no check point system. The down side to that is that you will be using the quick save/load feature constantly; sometimes over a dozen times just to get past one corner where soldiers are waiting to ambush you. There is absolutely no skill involved in this game what-so-ever. It is simply a matter of getting past an area, gaining a little bit of advancement, quicksaving, and repeating as you gradually progress little by little. The graphics, while terrible by today's standards and not very good for the standards of its release date, do a very effective job in recreating an oppressive, post-war soviet atmosphere. The game attempted to be accurate by implementing a critical hit system, which means that you can have 100% health, but one bullet in the right spot, (heart, head, ect.) can take it down to almost 0%. And trust me, there is an ocean of bullets flying at you. You'll find that this system works in your favor also as using your sniper weapon, (the most crucial firearm in the game) and zooming in for headshots is the most effective way to kill your enemies. It's a trial and error system that will have you dying A LOT!
So why am I recommending this game? One reason: The price. I got this game for two dollars on sale. For that price it was worth it. Do not pay a dollar more for this game. Deep inside of me, there is a perverse, masochistic streak that takes some sick pleasure in an occasional bad game, much like many people find watching a campy, low-budget movie entertaining. Also, I promise you will enjoy the cutscenes. Trust me on this. They are the most poorly translated, horrendously voice-acted cutscenes you will ever see in your life time. I enjoyed them immensely. If you can find this game for a dollar or two on sale, and you have nothing better to do, give it a try.

The game's fun--although strictly PvP. Those that play Chromehounds back in the day will probably like this, and as someone that played MW2 and 3 I've been largely happy with it.
The Good:
The mechs are gorgeous to look at, there's a good variety of mechs, and the F2P model isn't horrible. You can absolutely play the game without putting a single dime into the game, and perform on roughly equal footing. Real money generally gets you things that make the game more comfortable, but most of the time, it's not grossly pay to win, which is nice.
The gameplay is decent--about what you would expect. It's a team oriented game, and playing it with friends or unit members--particularly with a private VOIP, can be a blast.
The Bad:
It does get buggy, now and then, particularly in Faction Play--generally when respawning mechs. It can be annoying to have to exit the game and sign back in.
With only a few game modes and no story campaign, the game can get repetitive really quickly. This is more of an issue when you're playing solo, as the community is about what you would expect for a PvP game, but it's worth mentioning. Do yourself a favor and either look for units on mwomercs, or reach out to nogutsnogalaxy, or similar. The people you play with really make the game.
The Meh:
Game balance is....not perfect. Not surprising, but the big problem is balance for Clan tech vs IS tech--which becomes very obvious in Faction War--when the two sides are segregated by IS vs Clan. Quick Play it's a bit less of an issue. However, it's worth mentioning regardless.
Final Thoughts:
It's a great game if you have other people to play with--and a fun way to kill a couple hours in big stompy robots. It's definitely got a learning curve--both with mech design, and with actually playing the game, but it definitely feels good once you got a grip on things.
But again, try to find people to play ASAP. The game can be frustrating at times, especially if you're new, on your own, and your team's on a losing streak.

I bought this and the expansion for $1, played for about 3 hours, and I'm not sure I will pick it up again. I love the theme and universe of the game but the UI and gameplay are needlessly obtuse and repetitive.  There is too much clicking involved to get into and out of menus (click on a star system, click on a planet, select a thing for the planet to do, click out of the planet, click out of the star system, repeat with next star system/planet). A system like Attila TW for selecting provinces and then choosing upgrades from a panel at the bottom would be much better.   Combat is another weak area. I thought it would be really cool to make your own ships and choose 'cards' (tactics)  etc and it is...but it also is not:
There are so many meaningless combat skirmishes that take up loads of time. Half the time the AI retreats if it is outmatched which devolves into your fleet chasing a single ship (or worse, 3 ships that split up into 3 separate fleets) all around your interior. So you ignore those and move to take enemy planets, but then these small ships just camp there and blockade your planets and strangle your economy.  Overall I have found the game to be a big frustration.   Surprisingly there are a few annoying similarities between this and the total war series (like clicking 'end turn' over and over again) but I enjoy TW much more because the gameplay feels decisive and there is a sense of accomplishment, even though Im craving for a good space game.  I would recommend that prospective buyers buy Endless Legend instead,  or something like Sins of a Solar Empire.  Ultimately for $1 it was worth a shot but if I had paid full price I would be pretty regretful now, wishing I'd bought something like Stellaris instead.

Endless Space is a fun space 4x game that focuses on managment and large scale planning more than the finer details. This is my only experience in the space 4x genre so this review should be read from the perspective of a newbie.
With all of that said, Endless Space is a very fun game if you enjoy management and large scale planning in strategy and 4x games.  Much like the other Endless strategy games, Endless Space excells first and foremost in creating unique and varied experiences right from the start with well made, and very diverse factions to choose from.  From there, it is all about expanding, researching and building as you take over the galaxy.  All of which are very satisfying.
This game boasts a fairly nice level of complexity and balance which left me constantly experimenting with build paths and constantly learning how to play better.
The only down side I can see to this game, and this may be a deal breaker for some people, is that the combat sucks.  There is no micro management for combat.  Combat is essentially how you build your troops and then you can watch a cinematic of how the battle resolves.  Personally, I loved this as I find combat to be tedious in almost all strategy games, but those of you who enjoy building troops and leading them to victory: this game is not for you.
I loved this game.  If you are a fan of 4x strategy and don't mind forgoing a meaningful combat experience, this game offers a deep and fun experience that focuses on the macro side of things.  I am new to the Space subgenre of 4x but so far this game stands out as amazing.  (If you have micromange the crap out of your combat, this is a pass unfortunatly).

I guess it's easy to hate on SimCity with this review. We can go on all day about how♥♥♥♥♥♥that game was, but that'd be praising Cities In Motion 2 on the account of it's main competitor being ****. I won't do that. Instead, I'll relate to another game. One that has a lot more love.
I will relate this game to Transport Tycoon. Because this game is much more similar to that game in many respects.
Like TT, Cities In Motion is a game about building transport systems. The scale is limited to a large city rather than a large land, and the cargo variety is minimized to just passengers, but for the rest, it's very much like TT. And that's kind of that.
Beyond that, CiM2 has a lot of different stuff. You build stops and direct bus lines through them. One bus line may not yield much. But when that line links up to a different line, not necessarily a bus line, people along the second line will use the first line too if they need to go there. Passengers go places and your transport systems are there to help that be possible without needing to pick up a car.
The roadbuilding is very free-form. Just click a point, and then another, and it'll connect them with a straight line. Click a third point, and it'll create a nice curve. Keep clicking new points and you have a scribble. Or a long line. Or a long curve. Click the last point and the road is built. It's very simple.
However, this game has some problems of it's own. Let's start off with the biggest problem: stability. The game runs on Unity. And while Unity is pretty good at making decent games, it does suffer from a minor stability issue, where the game crashes due to a GetThreadContextException. If you save a lot, the game will remain manageable, and the progress loss will be minor, but it is a nuisance that is common in Unity games.
The UI may require a little direction, but is manageable once you've completed the tutorial. The tutorial does miss a few mechanics, though. For instance, you'll need to go to Reddit or the wiki to find out how to work with water buses and trolleys, although the latter is similar to the trams in many ways.
Then there's some missing features which'll leave most players going WTF MATES?! One thing I miss is the ability to change roads without having to demolish them.
Next, there's difficulty. While metros are a massive investment, if you get major corners of a city connected, you'll earn it all back in a single afternoon. In the days that follow, you spend most of your time getting rid of the passenger back-ups that are caused by the vast new amount of transport opportunities. And while you'd expect 50% coverage is an easy feat, it's surprisingly difficult. But with no competition and the lack of a loss condition, there is limited challenge.
The last complaint I have is the fact that at the moment (2014-03-23) I think some of the DLC has a fairly poor content/value balance. Furthermore, there's multiple packages that are very focused on owners of the older Cities In Motion. Despite that, some DLC does offer some nice changes. For instance, the Metro DLC completely overhauls the mechanics of the Metros, making the whole system a lot deeper. Fortunately, there is no vital DLC. The game is perfectly playable without any DLC. I do believe that the DLC offers a lot of options that are better than the standard options though.
Despite that, it has some nice things. For one, the world looks very good. I find it very relaxing to for instance just position my camera over a suburban surface railway station and just watch the trains come and go. Also, the passenger simulation has a great, but manageable level of detail. It quickly becomes noticeable if that multi-million dollar metro line was really worth covering the entire city for, but passengers use it and existing lines that barely made the cut have now become viable, so it probably is. You can get a lot of information about the state of your city and your company by looking at the data views, and some of that information can tell you very useful stuff, like if it's a good idea to use the highway, or to build a dedicated route, as well as if a line is likely to provide your system with a good amount of traffic.
On the whole, I think this is a good game. It has it's flaws, yes, like relatively high DLC prices, roads being impossible to upgrade without having to tear them down, and some other minor nuisances. But it's good looking, plays fairly well, and if you're a perfectionist and immense fan of making a perfect transport system, this'll keep you busy for hours.

Thirteen hours in the last few days, and I still can't quite figure out why I like this game. The graphics are, indeed 8-bit, though the colors are more like 16 bit. 32 bit if you play with the flesh tone color change option (/color <0-9>), as some of the variances are too subtle for 16 bit.
You can mod your textures very easily. Which, I did do... Since I was sick of blue glass that you couldn't see through and neon green grass that makes your eyes water. All it takes to mod is a zip file creator and a paint program with transparency.... Go check the community, there's a FAQ for that.
Some of the stuff you really want is limited to platinum, which is only available through real-world money. Though, there are people that buy plat items and sell them for gold. (Regular quest cash.) Maybe that's what I like about this game.... When I used to play all those 8 and 16 bit RPGs, I used to think to myself that I could make better houses. This is my chance. (And, yes, I am a fanatic for a certain game that starts with an 's' and ends with 'ims.')
Also, the game isn't that difficult. I find that making money is a breeze once you buy a gun and just sit just barely in range of a spawner. Levelling to 4 was long, but - if you do the draco and brain quests - not terribly bad. The draco quests can be repeated by clearing your quest log, by the way. I haven't hit 5 yet, but I'm on the way and looking forward to opening up some more blocks to build with. I'm also really looking forward to gathering enough gold to buy a spawner off of someone that has plat, so I can make a shooting range.

Sakura Agent
License to Creep
Developer: Winged Cloud
Year: 2017
Genre: Visual Novel, NSFW
Franchise: Sakura
Engine: Ren'Py
NOTICE
Welcome to a brand new, double stuffed Dan Peculiar special feature: "Dan Peculiar After Dark." A little while ago, I made a very questionable promise to my good friends. "Buy me a game," I said "And I'll play and review it!"
I said this because I seemingly value my limited time on this Earth very little and because I need to reach 500 games on steam in order to feel satisfied. So, much like Faust, I sold my soul for a bunch of Hentai games to pad my library. I keep my promises, however, so expect more reviews of these godawful games.
TL;DR
As you could guess, this is a creepy game. The writing and dialogue isn't strong enough to coast between the vaguely titillating still images and the graphics are nowhere near diverse enough to justify the asking price. If you want *satisfaction*, there are better and cheaper ways to get it than this horrible bizarre game.
Story
In this title you play as a lecherous sociopath working as a secret agent, but not cool or clever like James Bond. Your protagonist Akira is caught between the sensible Kimiko and the innocent goof-off Masumi, two girls who vie for his affections for some reason. The characters are cringe-inducingly blunt about everything and the dialogue is frequently very very stilted. Akira works for an agency that deal with "incursions", breaches of transdimensional creatures into our world. It's a cool concept that absolutely nothing is done with. As a matter of fact, we only ever see one of these creatures and it is of course a tentacle monster. The plot feels like an afterthought, and it flip-flops between scenes of killing aliens to scenes of Akira ogling the two girls competitively stripping for his amusement without so much as a change of music. The typical skeezy beats are here: Strip poker, beach trip and alien molestation, but I doubt it would even be enough to hold the attention of your average 12-year-old. The idea of a visual novel is to tell a story, not to baselessly excite. 3/10
Graphics
The art is good enough when it's there: The girls are well drawn and the backgrounds are nice. However, this is the extent of the art within the game. The girls switch between facial expressions occasionally but we never see the cool aliens or other characters or a n y t h i n g  i n t e r e s t i n g  a t  a l l. The game is frustratingly empty. 4/10
Gameplay
There is none, it's a visual novel. You click through the terrible dialogue and make about 3 choices in order to find more creepy shots of the girls. That's it. I don't mind the lack of gameplay engagement when the story is good, but it isn't. So I do. 5/10
Overall
Sakura Agent feels woefully undercooked in all facets. I really wish that I could say more, but it's so small. For the ridiculous price point the game becomes quite simply worthless. Don't even pick it up on sale, it's just not good. 3/10
